name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
summary: A quadruped mobility exercise that develops rotational range of motion in the thoracic spine while stabilizing the lumbar spine and pelvis.

setup: Start on all fours with your wrists stacked directly beneath your shoulders and your knees beneath your hips.
Engage your core to maintain a neutral, flat spine from pelvis to neck.
Place one hand behind your head or neck with the elbow pointed outward, keeping the supporting arm firmly planted.
steps: Rotate your upper torso down and inward, pointing the elevated elbow toward your opposite wrist or floor.
Reverse the movement by rotating your upper torso open toward the ceiling, driving the elbow upward as far as comfortable without shifting your hips.
Pause momentarily at the top of the rotation.
Smoothly return to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you rotate down across your body, and exhale as you rotate open toward the ceiling.
cues: Keep hips square to the floor
Rotate through your ribcage, not your lower back
Push the floor away with the supporting hand
Follow your elbow with your eyes

common_faults.fault: Shifting hips side to side to cheat rotation.
common_faults.correction: Keep your pelvis level and stationary; sit hips slightly back toward your heels if needed to lock the lumbar spine.

common_faults.fault: Pulling on the neck with the raised hand.
common_faults.correction: Rest your fingertips lightly behind your head without applying any forward or sideways pressure.
Actively press into the floor through the supporting palm to keep the chest proud and shoulder stable.

precautions: Move in a slow, controlled manner and avoid forcing rotational end range.
